row.description: Maven commonly writes a dependency coordinate as groupId:artifactId. The literal colon separates two identifiers. A wrong generalization would treat any punctuation-separated pair as equivalent, accepting slash-separated package paths or replacing the colon with a dot.

neighbors.relationship: Often extends this form with a version, as group:artifact:version.
Uses an optional @scope/name structure instead of a colon separator.

row.description: RFC 1945 HTTP/1.0 defines the closed request-method vocabulary GET, HEAD, and POST. A wrong generalization would extrapolate from newer HTTP versions and accept later methods such as PATCH or arbitrary uppercase tokens.

neighbors.relationship: Contains methods standardized after HTTP/1.0 as well as newer registered methods.
Is another HTTP token class, but it is numeric rather than a closed method lexicon.

row.description: A dotenv file is conventionally a repeated sequence of NAME=value assignments, one assignment per line. This restricted deployment profile uses uppercase environment names and unquoted simple values. A wrong generalization would model the file as one assignment only, or treat repeated lines as a free-form paragraph.

neighbors.relationship: Can use similar NAME=value syntax but has shell expansion and quoting semantics.
Uses repeated key-value entries but commonly groups them into named sections.

positives:
HOST=localhost
PORT=8080
API=enabled
LOG=debug
CACHE=redis_01
WORKER=worker2

row.description: Git accepts a unique hexadecimal object-name prefix; command output often shows seven or twelve characters, but the abbreviation width is variable and may need to grow to remain unique. A wrong generalization would freeze the apparent sample width at seven characters or require a full 40-character SHA-1.

neighbors.relationship: Uses the complete 40-character hexadecimal object name.
May append tag, distance, and dirty-state information around an abbreviated object ID.
